components.text: Northstar Dynamics uses a coordinated incident-response process to protect people, information, services, and legal obligations while preserving reliable evidence.

lines.text: Northstar Dynamics uses a coordinated incident-response process to protect people, information, services,
and legal obligations while preserving reliable evidence.

components.text: 2. Incident Response Checklist

1. Priority 1 incidents must be acknowledged within 15 minutes and assigned an incident commander who confirms severity and the immediate communication channel. 2. The initial containment target is 45 minutes, with deviations documented together with the operational reason and revised containment approach. 3. Open the incident bridge using +1-555-0147 and verify required responders can join before sensitive details are discussed. communications procedures. 5. Legal must be notified when regulated data exposure is suspected, even before the investigation confirms the affected record volume. 6. Evidence must be stored in the Orion Evidence Vault with timestamps, source attribution, and chain-of-custody information. 7. Create one incident record and link technical work items so chronology, ownership, decisions, and evidence remain traceable. 8. The incident commander must issue an initial executive update within 60 minutes, separating confirmed impact from unresolved uncertainty. 9. Separate confirmed facts from hypotheses and record the tests used to validate or reject significant investigative theories. 10. Restrict destructive remediation until evidence preservation is complete unless continued operation creates greater legal, safety, or security harm. 11. Assign a communications lead to coordinate internal messages and prevent inconsistent statements to employees, customers, suppliers, or regulators. 12. Customer notification requires approval from Legal and Corporate Communications before release, including audience timing, wording, and channel. 13. Track each containment action with an owner, timestamp, expected result, and rollback consideration so responders understand dependencies. 14. Validate restored systems against clean baselines and monitor for recurrence before declaring containment or recovery complete. 15. Incident records must be retained for seven years, including decisions, approvals, evidence references, communications, and final review records.

components.text: IV. Recovery Exercise Procedure
A. Preparation
Recovery exercises occur twice each calendar year. The exercise coordinator is Marcus Webb. Preparation confirms scope, participants, dependencies, safety constraints, and evidence responsibilities.

lines.text: Recovery exercises occur twice each calendar year. The exercise coordinator is Marcus Webb. Preparation
confirms scope, participants, dependencies, safety constraints, and evidence responsibilities.

components.text: - Confirm exercise objectives and participating services. - Validate contact lists and escalation paths. - Prepare evidence capture in Continuity Ledger.

lines.text: - Confirm exercise objectives and participating services.
- Validate contact lists and escalation paths.
- Prepare evidence capture in Continuity Ledger.

components.text: B. Execution
- Execute the approved scenario. - Observe recovery controls. - Capture technical evidence. - Record timestamps and validation results. - Capture business evidence. - Record owner approvals.
WARNING: Stop the exercise if simulated actions could cause uncontrolled production impact.

lines.text: WARNING: Stop the exercise if simulated actions could cause uncontrolled production impact.

components.text: C. Closure
Corrective actions are due within 30 calendar days. The exercise evidence repository is Continuity Ledger.
